reviews.text: When I ask my dog-owning friends who live in Tokyo, many say this hospital is the most trustworthy, and when I'm really in trouble, I go here. Not only do they provide accurate diagnoses and thorough examinations, but the hospitality of the reception staff is also excellent, making it a truly satisfying animal hospital.

On October 15th, 2026, my elderly cat visited the clinic. The previous evening, there was only one online appointment slot available, so I booked it for 5 PM. I struggled with my trembling cat, apologizing profusely, and managed to cram her into her carrier bag before heading there. Parking is just a short walk from the nearby Timez27.

Upon entering, I was greeted by a wonderful atmosphere, almost like a human hospital! The spacious entrance hall, with its smiling reception area, and the separate waiting rooms for dogs and cats, immediately boosted my positive impression.

Another positive point was the complete absence of that typical animal hospital smell. While dogs and cats are part of our family, even pet owners find that distinctive animal odor unpleasant. However, it's possible my nose was just stuffed up due to severe hay fever.

My name was called, and I entered the examination room for a consultation with the doctor. I was completely charmed by the doctor's thorough explanations, attentive service, and gentle approach to my cat. Needless to say, my positive impression of the clinic skyrocketed. After the examination, we received our medication. But the biggest plus point was the final payment. At animal hospitals, payment always takes a long time. The timid cat from before suddenly transformed into a fierce, glaring cat, radiating pressure as if to say, "Let's go!"

At other animal hospitals in the past, I'd imagine myself saying, "I'll come back tomorrow to pay!" while waiting, but here, all I had to do was scan the QR code on the medication slip at the payment machine. I could choose credit card or cash, and it was over in an instant. I was relieved from that waiting pressure... filled with a sense of accomplishment.

Finally, I noticed a "treat corner" in the entrance with treats like "Churu" for rewards after the examination. What a thoughtful service! There's also a water dispenser, so even those coming from far away can rest assured. My positive impression of this place just kept going up.


Dogs and cats can't tell us when they're in pain, suffering, or feeling unwell, so we pet owners go to the vet with a wary mindset, right? That's why we'd like to recommend this to pet owners like you.

Even if your pet doesn't need it right now, why not come in for a check-up, get a vaccination, and finish off with a treat?

I went to many different hospitals, but I finally settled on PECO.

They have doctors with excellent expertise in various fields, such as dentistry and neurology, so I feel like I can get a second opinion within the clinic.

Above all, they put the dog first and reduce the emotional burden, which means both my dog ​​and I experience less stress.

I'm so glad I found PECO.

(Posted from within the clinic)

The clear explanations put my family at ease.

I appreciate the thorough explanations regarding the medications I inquired about via LINE.

I would like to use their services again in the future if needed.

My Minuet cat underwent spaying surgery. Dr. Hosoya, who was in charge of the surgery, provided very thorough care from before to after, which made me feel at ease during my visits. He carefully explained my cat's condition and constitution before the surgery, and even explained what kind of stress the surgery might cause and provided information about aftercare. My small cat was small, and even the XS size post-operative suit that we had prepared was too big for her, but he kindly handmade a post-operative suit for her when she was discharged using a bandage-securing ramp. I was so grateful for his warm and caring approach. When I consulted him about things unrelated to the surgery, he gave me advice tailored to my cat's constitution, such as the frequency of shampooing and her food preferences, which I really appreciated.

My previous post seems to have disappeared, so I'm reposting it.

I used to go to the Harajuku main hospital, but last year I found a lump on my dog ​​and rushed him to the hospital for an examination. My usual vet wasn't there that day, so another veterinarian examined him. Without going into details, there was a discrepancy between the vet's explanation and my usual vet's opinion, which resulted in a delay in deciding on surgery. While I don't know if there's a direct causal relationship, the malignant tumor metastasized.

When I inquired about this with my usual vet, the group leader unexpectedly appeared and, without explanation, told me they could no longer treat my dog, forcing me to transfer to another hospital. I had been told beforehand that my usual vet was leaving Peco to go to another hospital, meaning appointments would be reduced to twice a month. Initially, the plan was for my dog ​​to be seen only during those two appointments, with another vet taking over on the other days. However, the situation suddenly changed.

Considering the burden of transferring my dog ​​in his final stages, I requested that even if the vet changed, they continue to treat him at the same hospital, but this was refused. We weren't trying to blame any medical malpractice; we just wanted an explanation of what happened. However, their response felt like an attempt to shirk responsibility.

Furthermore, despite agreeing to a transfer with the promise of a guaranteed referral to another hospital, the list of available hospitals provided consisted entirely of hospitals more than an hour's journey from our home. When we asked for a referral to a hospital that seemed somewhat accessible, it seemed there hadn't been a clear communication, and we were told they couldn't accept our child as a regular veterinarian.

Moreover, the list included hospitals with no doctors capable of treating our child's illness. Ultimately, we found a hospital ourselves.

Because of the nature of the illness, finding a new veterinarian took time. While they promised to continue seeing our child until a suitable one was found, when we requested an examination on a day when our child was ill, they refused and only sent medication. Frustrated, we contacted the operating company, but they seemed completely unaware of the concept of a duty to provide medical care.

Perhaps because the operating company is an advertising media company, our Google reviews are deleted every time we write them, and we've seen other low-rated comments deleted several times. Occasionally, when a low rating is given, a 5-star rating appears almost immediately to counteract it. Also, an account that has only commented once before suddenly posts a long comment with a photo. And they even got the name of the hospital wrong, claiming to be a dog lover who runs there every time. Where is Peso? (laughs) I don't know if it's true, but I found it very unnatural.

Their website boasts of state-of-the-art facilities and claims to be a caring, family-run hospital, but personally, I didn't feel that way at all. It seems like a hospital that turns its back on you when things don't go their way.

I'm very grateful to my current vet for treating my dog ​​without complaint, even though his condition was severe and they joined the hospital midway through treatment.
They were very kind to me.

I entrusted Dr. Hakozaki, an orthopedic surgeon, with the surgery on both of my dog's legs, which had patellar luxation grades 3-4, in March. The two-month follow-up examination went smoothly, and the consultations are now complete.

Dr. Hakozaki kept me updated with photos and updates via LINE after the surgery, which was very reassuring.

I later learned that this hospital has a specialist in anesthesia management, which I believe helps reduce the risks associated with anesthesia.

Now, my dog ​​has no exercise restrictions and is playing happily.

Thank you so much for your care.

The reception staff and doctors are all calm and kind.

Even on days I wasn't going to the hospital, I could consult with them via LINE, which was a great help mentally.

From routine care to advanced medical treatment.

Their motto is "We will be by your side for your pet's entire life," and that's exactly what they did.

Not only did they cure my pet's illness, but they also helped me mentally as a pet owner, and I'm truly grateful.

This is a highly recommended hospital where you can entrust your precious pet with peace of mind.

We have been receiving care since September 2021.

Our relationship with Dr. Ohno dates back to when he was an associate professor at the University of Tokyo.

Three years ago, she underwent surgery for pyometra and granulosa cell tumor.

At the end of March this year, she became unsteady on her legs, and on the way to the hospital, her head tilted. After arriving at the hospital, she experienced incontinence, vomiting, and a sudden deterioration in her condition. Dr. Ohno and Dr. Hosoya rushed to the hospital and took her to the treatment room.

Dr. Ohno said it was a disease originating from the brain or neck.

He said a neurologist was examining her.

He said a definitive diagnosis was needed with an MRI. I explained that general anesthesia was a bit risky for a 13-year-old, 10-month-old dog, but there were suspected diseases, including vertical and lateral nystagmus. The vertical nystagmus suggested a brain issue, leading to suspicion of a brain tumor or stroke. While it wasn't a definitive diagnosis, Dr. Kanno from the neurology department said treatment could begin, and I trusted his words and had treatment started immediately.

At the time of onset, she had paralysis in both hind legs, crawling and wearing diapers, but she recovered day by day. She was able to stop wearing diapers within a week, her nystagmus disappeared, and she could stand and walk on her own, albeit a little unsteadily.

Six months after the onset, although her neck is still tilted, she is living a normal life.

She saved my life twice.

In May, she turned 14, and I am grateful to Dr. Ohno, Dr. Kanno, and all the staff.

My pet and I are a troublesome family, but we ask for your continued support. 🙏

Additional post. 🙇‍♀️

One year and three months have passed since the brainstem infarction. Thanks to Dr. Kanno and the staff, she turned 15 last month.

Although her neck is still tilted, she has no paralysis, no recurrence, and is living a normal life.

At the time of onset, Dr. Ohno told me that a neurologist was examining her. I had no idea that there were veterinary neurologists in the animal world.

Sacchan is a Shiba Inu. Vestibular disorders are very common in this breed.

I hope that through Sacchan's posts, people will learn that there are veterinarians who specialize in neurology.

I was allowed to film a video of a neurological examination and abdominal ultrasound (because gastric stasis occurred after the onset of symptoms).

Thank you, Dr. Kanno, for your cooperation.

Sacchan has turned 15, making her equivalent to 76 years old. Various illnesses are possible in the future, so we take her for checkups once a month for early detection.

A year for a human is only three months for a dog.

I recommend health checkups even when your dog is healthy, not just when they are unwell.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused by our aging dog, Sacchan and I.

Thank you for your continued support.

Our dogs absolutely adore Dr. Nagahama and run to the hospital every time we visit.

Not only is he incredibly knowledgeable, but he always speaks to our dogs kindly, saying things like, "You're so cute!" during examinations, so we feel completely at ease leaving them in his care.

We have complete trust in the doctors.

We're so glad we found such a wonderful hospital like Peso.

I am truly grateful to have found this hospital. Originally, the branch hospital was closer to my home, but I needed surgery, so I started going to the main hospital. The equipment, specialists, and staff are like those in a family hospital, and everyone treated me very kindly when I was hospitalized. I will continue to visit for regular checkups, and I can't imagine going to any other hospital.

Several years ago, when the clinic first opened, my beloved dog received treatment there. As a pet owner, I felt that my dog ​​was nearing the end of his life, but the clinic seemed to prioritize life-prolonging, aggressive treatment, telling me that he would die if he didn't eat or receive treatment. I understand the desire to help animals live as long as possible. However, I think that aggressive treatment for a dog in the final stages of life who had stopped eating only caused him more pain. I spent many days agonizing over what the right thing to do for my dog ​​was, and I wish there had been a system in place for end-of-life support. But they were kind to my dog ​​until the very end. Thank you.

A good doctor,
cheerful staff,
abundant amenities,
space designed with visitor flow in mind,
a place that makes patients with tails want to go,
gentle treat perks,
one-touch payment system, and more.

By registering on LINE via your mobile phone, you can make appointments and discuss symptoms.

The following store is temporarily closed, so please use it as a reference.

In the area on your way home, dogs are allowed inside:

[Cafe Dining Da-ism*]

Features vegan menus mainly using vegetables and soybeans.

Of course, there are also dishes for hungry and playful dogs.

(^^)

Since 2024, restaurants that allow dogs with tails to dine inside have appeared (^o^) It's a great help.

Most restaurants in the Omotesando, Harajuku, and Poplar Avenue area only allow dogs on the terrace.

It was less than a 10-minute walk from the hospital.

If you are bringing a large dog, please call ahead to confirm seating arrangements.

From here, as a record of past articles from Hospital Peco:

It seems there is a consulting firm with the same name in the same building, so perhaps this animal center is constantly evolving, incorporating ongoing improvements in treatment and I-DeA (In-De-A)?

The system for reducing stress for patient dogs and cats, and for easing the worries of accompanying parents, is truly impressive.

Of course, everyone has a relationship with their local veterinarian, so this hospital might be worth visiting once on an occasion.

However, in case of emergency, those living on the east side of the Yamate area should consider searching for the Japan Animal Medical Center*, located behind the New National Theatre, with a parking lot right in front of the building, a beautifully rebuilt facility, and excellent inpatient facilities.
m(_ _)m I deeply admire everyone who sincerely handles the high-risk, 24-hour, rapidly changing nature of their work.

For my mother dog's final care, although it was a bit far, we went to Nippon Veterinary and Life Science University* (of course, any well-known university-affiliated veterinary hospital nearby would also be fine). Our then-family veterinarian wrote a referral letter, and we received detailed examinations and symptomatic treatment as a second opinion.
We fought together for several years, alongside future veterinarians, until she crossed the rainbow bridge.

I would be very happy if I could be of any help in their treatment or in providing empirical knowledge about their pathology.

Dear Mr./Ms. Hiroshi Nakajo,

Thank you very much for your kind and high rating of our hospital.

We sincerely apologize for the delay in our response.

We will continue to strive to be a hospital that you and your family can use with peace of mind.

Please feel free to contact us anytime if you have any concerns or problems.

We look forward to your continued patronage.

Peco Animal Medical Center, Harajuku

We always have our cat (Kotoha) examined at this hospital.

The hospital has a LINE account, which makes it easy to contact them if we have any concerns about symptoms, if we can't make our scheduled appointment, or if an unexpected problem causes a delay.

Also, they give us a Churu treat at the hospital, which seems to have eased our cat's fear of the vet a little.

Thank you for your continued support!

Dear shigeru1024,

Thank you very much for your kind and high praise of our hospital.

We also sincerely apologize for the delay in our response.

We are extremely pleased to receive such praise, and it is a great source of encouragement for all of our staff.

We will continue to strive to be a hospital where everyone can feel at ease consulting with us.

Please feel free to speak to any of our staff members at any time if you have any concerns or problems.

We look forward to your continued patronage.

Peco Animal Medical Center Harajuku

A beautiful veterinary hospital close to Harajuku Station.
Parking is available at the nearby Times, and a service voucher can be used to cover up to 1,800 yen (per hour).
Each hospital has a specialist, and they will provide explanations and treatment methods while respecting your opinion and making suggestions.
As each veterinarian is assigned to you, there is no need to worry about a different veterinarian each time you visit, which is very reassuring.
You can consult with them anytime via LINE, and they respond quickly.
At night, they are treated at the affiliated TRVA Animal Medical Center in Yoga.
I only used them once, but as they are an affiliated hospital, they were quick to respond and all treatment details were shared with me, so I felt at ease.

Above all, the facilities are well-equipped, so I don't have to worry about being passed around from one hospital to another, and I can rely on them as my regular doctor.
While hospitals aren't places where customer service skills are required, the reception staff are very polite and I get the impression that they provide thorough employee training.
